title: The Downward Fall of the Sinner
english: weapons of light. It is carried in the manuscripts instead of 'they brought down Israel,' as 'they led Israel down,' showing also by this word that the one sinning is brought from on high to below. And many are the writings that show this, such as: 'How has the morning star fallen from heaven, rising in the morning?' (Isaiah 14:12) and: 'They shall enter into the lowest parts of the earth' (Psalm 18:6). And other myriad words are revealing that the diligent ascends and is elevated, but the lover of pleasure descends, having a material choice, as to become 'fleshly, having been shaped by sin.'

I read an explanation of someone having taken that the four builders are the four evangelists. Whether it is so, let those encountering the one who wrote thus judge. It is possible to say the four builders are 'to gather the sent angels to gather the elect of God from the four winds,' that is, from the four climates of the inhabited world. In order that the four builders might be understood, they are shown and led by the Forethinker of all things, God, against those lifted up with audacity and arrogance, and against those having fallen by God's judgment, not lifting up the head, neither of the captor nor of the captives, the holy builders being set in opposition. It is also worn away in custom that those acting badly do not lift up the head.

And if the mind is sometimes signified by the name of the head, even this is not lifted up when someone 'is delivered to an unapproved mind, having not tested God to have in knowledge' (Romans 1:28). For how can he who has been held in an unapproved mind still think of the things above or split the heart in heaven, not having treasured in heaven? It corresponds to the scattering of Israel being recognized or being led away, that which is announced with full force by those having scattered against those having seized by force: 'Our bones have been scattered by the underworld' (Psalm 142:10). Since it seems the prophetic word is poured out from an unsuitability of composition, it should be changed thus—

Zechariah 2:5-6: And I lifted my eyes and saw; and behold a man, and in his hand a geometric cord. And I said to him: Where are you going? And he said to me: To measure Jerusalem, to see how great its breadth is, and how great its length. It has already been shown many times how one lifts the eyes of the inner man for the understanding of fitting spectacles. In the same manner as what was said, even now the prophet, lifting his eyes, saw a man holding in his hand a geometric cord, for the purpose, as a most excellent architect, of measuring how great the breadth and length of Jerusalem is, so that, the foundations being laid, its rebuilding may take place after it suffered demolition by enemies. Who the man seen by the prophet is, it is time to see. And see whether he is not the same as 'the one mounted on a red horse, standing between two shady mountains' (Zechariah 1:8).
